title: Trigger Management & Bulk Load Disabling
description: Enable, disable, rename, and drop triggers, and avoid trigger execution during mass data migrations.

data.text: During mass data migrations or initial ETL ingestion, triggers can degrade bulk load performance or fire unintended side effects. PostgreSQL allows disabling and enabling triggers cleanly.

data.title: Disabling Triggers for Bulk Ingestion
data.content: Temporarily disabling triggers on a table.

data.text: Inspecting Every Trigger on a Table

The catalog view `pg_trigger` lists every trigger, and joining to `pg_class` and `pg_proc` shows which table it is attached to and which function it calls. Checking this before a large data migration tells you exactly which triggers you are about to disable and re-enable.

data.title: List triggers with their function and enabled state
data.content: `tgenabled` is 'O' for enabled in origin, 'D' for disabled, and other values for replica-only firing.
data.code:
SELECT
    c.relname      AS table_name,
    t.tgname       AS trigger_name,
    p.proname      AS function_name,
    t.tgenabled,
    pg_get_triggerdef(t.oid) AS definition
FROM pg_trigger AS t
JOIN pg_class AS c ON c.oid = t.tgrelid
JOIN pg_proc  AS p ON p.oid = t.tgfoid
WHERE NOT t.tgisinternal
ORDER BY c.relname, t.tgname;

data.title: Disabling triggers disables integrity checks
data.text: `ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER ALL` also disables internal triggers, including those that enforce foreign keys. That is why it requires superuser and why it should only wrap a controlled load that you know is consistent. Prefer disabling named user triggers one at a time, and always re-enable them in the same transaction as the load so a failure cannot leave the table unprotected.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER` to pause trigger execution.
Always re-enable triggers immediately after data ingestion completes.
